## In plain words

This method does not learn from the book at all. Each knitted row is computed from the row before it by one tiny rule: every stitch looks at itself and its two neighbours in the previous row and decides whether it is a stitch or background. The motif stitches are written back in every row, so the motifs seed the patterns that flow out of them.

Different rules give completely different worlds: some make nested triangles, some regular lattices, some chaos. Knitting row by row makes this a natural fit for a machine.

## The setting

**The rule number.** There are 256 possible rules, numbered 0 to 255. Rule 90 makes nested triangles, rule 150 makes denser geometric lattices, and rule 30 is famously chaotic.
